column2: Welcome to Monster Meadow! Three little monsters want a friend. Who do you pick?
Your friend is hungry! Each crate holds ten berries. How many berries are here?
Your friend has twenty-three berries. Here come fourteen more. How many now?
Your friend has twenty-seven berries. Here come fifteen more. How many now?
Your friend has forty-six berries, and eats twelve. How many are left?
Your friend has fifty-two berries, and eats twenty-seven. How many are left?
Look at the rows of berries. Which one matches the picture?
Twelve berries, shared by three friends. Which one matches the picture?
You have a new friend! Tap your friend to say hello.
Does your friend need a new name? Type one, or keep this one.
Your friend is hungry! Tap the berries to feed your friend.
Nice. Now let us see what you two can do together.
Quick break! Give your partner a high five.
Answer what you can. If you are not sure, that is okay. Just press, Not sure.
A cart holds one hundred berries. A crate holds ten. How many berries are here?
The berries are shared equally. How many does each friend get?
Look at the groups of berries. Which one matches the picture?
How much of the bar is purple?
Which one is the same amount?
You made your first friend! Now let us go find more monsters.
This is your meadow. Something is hiding in the tall grass. Go and say hi!
Your egg is ready to hatch! Tap it!
Your egg needs to get warm. Every right answer warms it up.
Your egg hatched! Say hello to your new friend!
This friend wants to play with you today!
That is all of today done! Your first partner earned a bonus star. Come back tomorrow for more.
No berries left. Play a game to earn more!
This is your buddy now! Your buddy helps you, and teaches you new things.
So full! No more berries today.
Who could it be? Go and look!
You met this one. Keep going to make friends!
A wild monster! It loves plus treats.
A wild monster! It loves minus treats.
A wild monster! It loves times treats.
A wild monster! It loves sharing treats.
Pick a number, then a sign, then another number.
You found that one already. Try a new one!
True! But your friend has had that kind of easy treat.
A flip! Same parts, other way round.
True! That is a flip of one you have.
That works. But that is a lot of plus treats. Try another kind!
That works. But that is a lot of minus treats. Try another kind!
That works. But that is a lot of times treats. Try another kind!
That works. But that is a lot of sharing treats. Try another kind!
True! That is the easy one. Can you make a trickier treat?
Almost ready! This monster loves plus treats. Make one with plus.
Almost ready! This monster loves minus treats. Make one with minus.
Almost ready! This monster loves times treats. Make one with times.
Almost ready! This monster loves sharing treats. Make one with the share sign.
You cannot share into zero groups. Try another number.
That does not share evenly. Some are left over.
Not that one. Look at the bars and try again.
Start with this number. How many more do you need?
Start with this number. How many do you take away?
Look at the rows of berries. How many are in each row?
Look at the groups of berries. How many groups are there?
You found so many! Try any numbers you like.
Keep going! Your friend still wants treats.
Your turn! Make one more with plus, all by yourself, with new numbers.
Your turn! Make one more with minus, all by yourself, with new numbers.
Your turn! Make one more with times, all by yourself, with new numbers.
Your turn! Make one more with sharing, all by yourself, with new numbers.
Your turn! Make one more your own way, all by yourself, with new numbers.
You did it all by yourself! Bonus hearts!
Your friend grew up! Look how big and strong!
That was so much fun! Your friend is full of stars for today. More stars tomorrow!
A match! Take away their power with your moves.
The move missed. Look at the bar, and try again.
Not yet. Look at the bar, and try again.
Take it in small steps. Tens first, then ones.
Let me show you. Type the answer you see.
Your power move is ready! Press the power button.
You won the match! Good game!
Put the berries together. Then count the crates and the loose berries.
Click the berries to feed your friend. Then count what is left.
So many loose berries! Ten fit in a crate. Pack a crate.
Now count the crates and the loose berries.
Packed! Ten berries made one new crate. Now count.
Ten crates made one cart. That is one hundred!
Packed back into a crate. Now count what is left.
One crate opened. Now there are ten more loose berries.
Your friend is full. Count what is left.
A whole crate is too much. Open a crate to get loose berries.
All eaten! How many are left? Count them.
No loose berries left. Open a crate!
Look at the loose berries. Ten of them fit in a crate. Pack a crate, then count again.
There are not enough loose berries. Open a crate to get more.
So close! Check which number is crates, and which is loose berries.
More berries are coming, so the pile grows. Put them together.
Your friend is eating berries, so the pile shrinks. Feed your friend, and count what is left.
So close! Count the berries one more time.
So close! Count the crates one more time.
Not yet. Let us use the berries to find out.
Not yet. Count the crates, then the loose berries.
Not yet. Put the berries together and count.
Not yet. Here are the berries to help.
Time for a tiny lesson. Watch me first!
Not quite. Look at the picture, and try again.
Here is the answer. Look at the picture, and count with me.
Every number is made of parts. Here is twelve.
I can break it into ten and two. Ten plus two makes twelve.
Or six and six. A double!
I can also start bigger, and take some away. Fifteen minus three.
Your turn. Seven, and how many more, to make twelve?
Monsters love treats with real parts. Plus zero is true, but it is the easy one. Try bigger parts!
Watch me add. Twenty-seven berries, and fifteen more.
I put them together. Three crates, and twelve loose berries. That is too many loose ones!
Ten loose berries fit in one crate. I pack ten. Now there are four crates, and two loose berries.
Four crates and two loose berries is forty-two.
Your turn. Thirty-six and eighteen. Too many loose berries. Press, pack ten.
How many berries now? Count the crates, then the loose ones.
You packed a crate! Grown-ups call that regrouping.
Watch me take away. Fifty-two berries. My friend eats twenty-seven.
First the crates. Two crates gone.
Now seven loose berries. But there are only two! So I open a crate.
Now I can take seven. Two crates and five loose berries are left. Twenty-five.
Your turn. Forty-three, take away eighteen. One crate is gone. Now eight loose berries, but there are only three. Press, open a crate.
Now eight can go. How many berries are left? Count the crates, then the loose ones.
You opened a crate! That is how to take away when there are not enough loose ones.
Look. Berries in rows. Three rows, with four berries in each row.
I could count four, and four, and four. That is twelve.
A faster way to say it: three times four. Three rows of four makes twelve.
Turn it around: four rows of three. Still twelve! Four times three is the same as three times four.
Your turn. Two rows of five. Which treat matches?
How many berries is two times five?
Twelve berries, and three friends. Everyone gets the same.
I share them out, one each, until they are gone. Each friend gets four.
We say: twelve divided by three is four.
Look, it is the rows again! Three rows of four is twelve. Sharing is times, backwards.
Your turn. Ten berries, two friends. Which treat matches?
How many does each friend get?
Let us do it together. First, put the berries together.
More than nine loose berries. Ten of them go in a crate.
Let us do it together. First, feed the crates.
Not enough loose berries. So we open a crate.
Now count. Crates first, then the loose berries. Pick the numbers below.
Welcome to Honey Hollow! The monsters here love honey bars, cut into equal pieces.
A wild monster! It loves honey.
How much of the honey bar is gold? Pick how many pieces are gold, and how many pieces there are in all.
How much of the bar is gold?
Fill the honey bar to make this fraction.
First cut the bar into equal pieces. Then fill it to make this fraction.
Which bar has more honey? Or are they the same?
Fill the bottom bar, so it has the same amount of honey as the top bar.
Your friend eats the same piece of honey bar every day. How much is that in all? Press, add a piece, to find out.
Your friend wants a piece of a piece. First cut the tray one way. Then cut it the other way.
How much of the whole tray is that?
All the pieces are down. Count them. The pieces are still the same size.
That is the first piece, in gold. Now take a part of the gold.
The dark gold is the piece of the piece. Count the dark pieces. Then count all the small pieces in the tray.
Let us count together. The gold pieces go on top. The pieces in one whole go on the bottom.
Let me help. Tap the pieces that glow.
Here are the bars to help.
So close! The bottom number is how many pieces in all. The top number is how many are gold.
Count the gold pieces, not the empty ones.
The bottom number counts all the pieces, gold and empty together.
Not yet. Count the pieces in the whole bar. Then count the gold ones.
Look at the bottom number. That is how many equal pieces the bar needs.
Look at the top number. That is how many pieces to fill.
A bigger bottom number means more cuts. More cuts make smaller pieces.
Not yet. Look at how far the gold goes in each bar.
Not yet. Make the gold go just as far as in the top bar.
The pieces stay the same size, so the bottom number stays the same. Only the top number grows.
It is times, not plus. Count every piece you put down.
Not yet. Put the pieces down, and count them.
Do not add the bottom numbers. Count all the small pieces in the whole tray.
That is only one of the two cuts. Cut the tray both ways, and count.
Not yet. Cut the tray both ways. Then count the dark pieces, and all the small pieces.
Here is one whole honey bar.
I cut it into four equal pieces. Every piece is the same size.
I fill one piece with honey. That is one fourth of the bar.
The bottom number says how many equal pieces are in the whole bar. The top number says how many are gold.
Now three pieces are gold. Three fourths.
Your turn. How many equal pieces are in this whole bar?
And how many pieces are gold?
Two thirds! Two gold pieces, out of three.
This honey bar is cut in two. One half is gold.
This bar is the same size, but cut in four. Two fourths are gold.
Look! The gold goes just as far. One half, and two fourths, are the same amount.
Now one half, and one fourth. Four is a bigger number than two. But one fourth is a smaller piece!
Your turn. Which one is more honey?
Yes. Thirds are bigger pieces than sixths.
My friend eats one fourth of a honey bar every day.
After two days, that is two pieces. Two fourths.
After three days, three pieces. Three times one fourth is three fourths.
The pieces stay the same size, so the bottom number stays the same. Only the top number grows.
Five days is five pieces. That is more than one whole bar!
Your turn. Two times one third. How many pieces are gold?
Two thirds. Two pieces, and each piece is one third.
Here is a whole tray of honey. I cut it into three equal strips, and fill one. One third.
My friend wants half of that third. So I cut the tray across, into two.
Half of the gold strip is this one small, dark piece.
How big is it? Count all the small pieces in the tray. Six. So it is one sixth.
Your turn. Half of one fourth. How many small pieces are in the whole tray?
One half of one fourth is one eighth. A piece of a piece is a smaller piece.
Ooh, a tricky one! Give it a try. If it is too hard, we will do it together.
Wow! That was a tricky one, and you got it!
That one was extra tricky. Let us look at it together.
You are getting stronger! The problems grow with you.
Level up! Your friend gets a bonus star.
A new monster is watching you! Play a bit more with your friends, and it will come out.
Spend your berries here! Charms are for your monsters. Decorations go in your meadow.
Got it! It is yours now.
Not enough berries yet. Play to earn more!
Your new decoration is in the meadow. Drag it to where you want it.
You got a charm! Tap a friend in the meadow, and press Charm, to put it on.
When you are done playing, press Good night, to tuck everyone in.
Good night, everyone! See you tomorrow.
Rise and shine! Everyone is awake.
These berries need counting! Tap a berry when you count it.
Fill the basket. Put in this many berries.
How many more berries make five?
A crate holds ten berries. How many more fill the crate?
One full crate, and some loose berries. How many berries in all?
Ten berries go in a crate. How many loose berries are left?
Each crate holds ten berries. How many berries are here?
Make this number, with crates and loose berries.
What is ten more than this number?
What is ten less than this number?
Let us count together. Touch each berry once.
Count each berry as it goes in the basket.
Here they are, side by side. Which row goes further?
Look at the crates first. More crates is more.
The crate is ten. Count on from ten.
Count the crates. Then count the loose berries.
Ten more is one more crate. The loose berries stay the same.
Ten less is one crate less. The loose berries stay the same.
So close! Touch each berry once as you count.
Line them up, side by side. Which one goes further?
Fewer means not as many. Look again.
Those are the berries that are there. Count the empty spots.
That is how many fit in all. Count only the ones that are missing.
A crate holds ten berries. Count the crate as ten, then count on.
So close! Crates come first, then the loose berries.
Let me show you. Look, then press Check.
Here are some berries. I touch each one, and say one number.
The last number I say is how many there are. Five berries.
It does not matter which berry I start with. It is still five.
Your turn. Count each berry once. How many are there?
Seven! The last number you say is how many.
Two piles of berries. Which has more?
I line them up, side by side.
This row goes further. Six is more than four.
The other row has fewer. Fewer means not as many.
Yes. Eight is more than five.
A crate holds ten berries. This crate has six.
I count the empty spots. One. Two. Three. Four.
Here is a full crate, and three loose berries. Ten, and three more, is thirteen.
Your turn. This crate has seven. How many more fill it?
Each crate holds ten berries. Three crates. Ten, twenty, thirty.
The first number says how many crates. The second number says how many loose berries.
Four crates and three loose berries is forty-three. The same two numbers, but a different amount!
Your turn. How many berries? Count the crates first.
Twenty-six. Two crates, and six loose berries.
Welcome to the Bakery! The monsters here love warm buns.
Buns in equal rows. How many buns in all?
Share the buns fairly. How many go in each basket?
Share the buns fairly. How many in each basket? And how many are left?
Put the slices together. How much of a loaf is that?
Some slices get eaten. How much of the loaf is left?
A full tray is one. How much is here?
Put them together. How much in all?
Some gets eaten. How much is left?
Look. Each part of the tray shows its buns. Add the parts.
Look. Every basket gets the same. Count one basket.
Share the big part first. Then share the rest.
The slices are the same size now. Count them.
The crossed slices are eaten. Count what is left.
A strip is one tenth. A small square is one hundredth.
Look at the trays. Which one is fuller?
Ten strips fill a tray. Count the full trays first, then the strips.
The crossed squares are eaten. Count what is left.
Cut! Now the slices are the same size.
So close! Those are tens. Look at the trays of ten again.
These are equal rows. That is times, not plus.
One part is not right yet. Look at that part again.
The parts are right! Add them up one more time.
That is how many are left. How many are in each basket?
You can still share those. Every basket can get one more.
We are sharing. Each basket gets less than the whole pile.
So close! Count one basket again.
The slices stay the same size. Only the top numbers are added.
The slices are not the same size yet. Cut the loaf to match first.
Start with the first loaf. Take the second one away from it.
Look at the sign again. Is it plus, or take away?
A strip is one tenth. A small square is one hundredth. Look again.
More digits does not mean more. Look at the tenths first.
Tenths go with tenths. Hundredths go with hundredths.
Ten strips fill a whole tray. That makes one.
Not yet. Let us use the picture to find out.
A tray of buns. Three rows of twelve. I split it in a tens part, and a ones part.
The tens part is three rows of ten. That is thirty.
The ones part is three rows of two. That is six.
I add the parts. Thirty and six is thirty-six.
Your turn. Four rows of thirteen. The parts are forty, and twelve. How many buns in all?
Fifty-two! A big tray is easy in parts.
Forty-eight buns, and four baskets. Every basket gets the same.
First I share the trays of ten. Each basket gets one tray. That is ten.
Then I share the eight loose buns. Each basket gets two more.
Ten and two is twelve. Forty-eight divided by four is twelve.
Your turn. Fourteen buns, four baskets. Each basket gets three. How many are left?
Two are left. Not enough to give every basket one more.
A loaf cut in four slices. One slice here, and two slices there.
The slices are the same size. So I just count them. One and two is three fourths.
Now one half, and one fourth. The slices are not the same size!
I cut the half again. One half is two fourths.
Your turn. Two fourths and one fourth. How many fourths is that?
Three fourths. Same size slices first. Then count.
This full tray is one. It has one hundred small squares.
A strip is ten squares. Ten strips fill the tray. One strip is one tenth.
Three strips is three tenths. We write zero point three.
One small square is one hundredth. Four strips and seven squares is zero point four seven.
Your turn. Which one is more?
Yes. Five strips is more than four strips and five squares.
